query: For the paper "Unfolding and Shrinking Neural Machine Translation Ensembles" (arXiv: 1704.03279), answer this question: What were the performance results of their network?

drafts:
Their best results on Japanese–English either yield a gain of 2.2 BLEU compared to the original single NMT network at about the same decoding speed, or a 3.4× CPU decoding speedup with only a minor drop in BLEU [4][9].

The method unfolds an ensemble of multiple NMT systems into a single large network and then shrinks it by removing redundant neurons [4]. Depending on the aggressiveness of shrinking, they could reduce the unfolded network to the size of the single NMT network while keeping the BLEU boost from the ensemble [9]. Note that the passages only report these headline numbers for the Japanese–English task; no comparable headline results for English–German are given in the provided excerpts.

cited_sources.text: 6 Conclusion We have described a generic method for improv- ing the decoding speed and BLEU score of single system NMT. Our approach involves unfolding an ensemble of multiple systems into a single large neural network and shrinking this network by re- moving redundant neurons. Our best results on Japanese-English either yield a gain of 2.2 BLEU compared to the original single NMT network at about the same decoding speed, or a 3.4× CPU de- coding speed up with only a minor drop in BLEU.

We report that with a mix of the presented shrinking methods we are able to reduce the size of the unfolded network to the size of the single NMT network while keep- ing the boost in BLEU score from the ensemble. Depending on the aggressiveness of shrinking, we report either a gain of 2.2 BLEU at the same de- coding speed, or a 3.4× CPU decoding speed up with only a minor drop in BLEU compared to the original single NMT system.
